source.title: Epiplexity Guided Data Selection and Generation for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
source.authors: Ellen Su; Andres Potapczynski; Shi-Kai Qiu; Edward Hughes; Andrew Gordon Wilson

record.file_problem: No apparent problem; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses fitted scaling laws to guide data selection, but does not test the claim's held-out loss scaling, large-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper fits cross-domain power laws to observed per-domain training losses and reports fit quality, but this is not a test of held-out pretraining loss scaling or prediction of much larger runs. Its downstream results relate epiplexity to task performance, not scale or pretraining loss to task performance. The selector and generation performance tables therefore do not test a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses online power-law fits of per-domain training loss versus tokens (Eq. 3, after ADO) as a tool for data selection. It reports only the fit quality of its own selector's scaling law (Appendix C.1) and downstream accuracy of its methods. It does not test whether held-out pretraining loss follows a power law across orders of magnitude, extrapolates to larger runs, or yields a compute-optimal allocation. The two model sizes (124M, 1.3B) in Table 1 compare selection methods on downstream accuracy, not loss scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that higher epiplexity predicts better OOD downstream generalization. They also conclude that EpiSelect, which uses scaling-law-forecast epiplexity gain, beats Natural and ADO at 124M and 1.3B on Common Pile. EpiGen, epiplexity-rewarded synthetic data generation, improves GLUE over pretrained GPT-2. They judge their scaling-law fits reliable for domain selection and that Pile is saturated as a selection benchmark. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws as such.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits online cross-domain power laws to per-domain training loss for data selection; it does not reproduce the original joint parameter, token, and compute scaling measurements or their compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports refitting every 1,000 iterations and specifies fitting initialization and constraints, but does not compare alternative fitting choices to assess their effects.

fits_no_version.finding: In one Common Pile run, cross-domain power-law fits track observed per-domain training-loss trajectories: median R2 0.88, log-RMSE 0.02 nats at the final step. Fits are weaker on three near-flat, noisy domains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online cross-domain power-law fits approximate in-run per-domain training-loss trajectories well enough to guide domain selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five Pile domain-trained 124M models, epiplexity correlates with mean zero-shot accuracy (r = 0.88, ρ = 0.90); weight norm does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epiplexity of training data predicts downstream zero-shot accuracy across data domains.

record.problems: The fit assessment is against observed trajectories rather than held-out data, and is reported for one run. The epiplexity-accuracy association covers only five domain-trained models. The paper notes lower fit quality for three near-flat, noisy domains.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the extraction limit. Other training and downstream performance tables do not measure any listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute against held-out loss; only in-run training-loss fits as a selection tool.
All: no prediction of larger runs from small ones.
All: domain weights are optimised, not the parameter/token split at fixed compute.
All: no comparison of shapes at fixed parameter count.
All: text only. The synthetic-data RL training is not analysed for power-law form.
All: downstream accuracy is related to epiplexity and selection method, not to scale or loss.
All: fitting choices are specified but not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is confirmed. The scaling law is a forecasting tool inside the selector; its reported accuracy is the method's own performance.

versions.untested_parts: The reported fits are to observed training losses, not held-out pretraining loss; no sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
No prediction from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger is reported.
Domain sampling weights are selected; the study does not find a loss-minimizing parameter-count/token-count allocation at fixed compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of the claimed power-law form across other modalities or training regimes.
The study relates epiplexity to downstream results, not scale or pretraining loss to downstream performance.
The study describes fitting choices but does not test whether exponents or compute-optimal splits change with setup, nor whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: LLaMA 2 family decoder-only transformer run (the particular model size is not identified)
rows.operation_detail: Fit cross-domain loss scaling laws to observed per-domain losses and token counts during training.
rows.measure: Median coefficient of determination and median log-RMSE for fitted versus observed per-domain loss trajectories
rows.note: The paper says R2 rises to 0.9 within the first 4k steps and then remains stable. Three domains had slightly lower R2; these had near-flat, noisy loss curves. These are fits to observed trajectories, not held-out or large-run extrapolation results.
rows.check: This is the fit quality of the study's own method component: a cross-domain law refit every 1,000 steps to in-run training-loss trajectories, for one run. It is not an independent test of V1 or V2. The model size for this run is not stated in C.1.

rows.subject: 124M LLaMA 2 family models trained separately on five Pile domains (aggregate correlation)
rows.operation_detail: Measure the association between per-domain epiplexity and mean zero-shot downstream accuracy across the domain-trained models.
rows.measure: Correlation of epiplexity with mean downstream accuracy
rows.value: Pearson r = 0.88, two-tailed p = 0.05; Spearman ρ = 0.90
rows.note: Aggregate result across five domain-trained models. This concerns epiplexity as a predictor, not scaling with parameters, tokens, compute, or pretraining loss.
rows.check: The row correlates epiplexity, a data property, with downstream accuracy across five domain-trained 124M models. Scale and pretraining loss are not varied, so it does not bear on V6. The p-value is reported as p ≈ 0.05.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
